description.narrative:
The project aims to alleviate the humanitarian crisis faced by IDPs in Port-au-Prince, particularly at Lycée Marie Jeanne and Faculté Linguistique Appliquée. Its primary objective is to improve IDP households' living conditions and food security, ease overcrowding in educational institutions, and ultimately facilitate a return to normal school operations. By addressing urgent food and hygiene needs, the project supports IDP well-being and helps stabilize educational infrastructure. The project will implement targeted interventions to meet the immediate needs of IDPs, with a focus on:
Cash Assistance: Provide two cash transfers to 400 households (2,000 individuals) for essential food and other urgent needs, covering 75% of the Minimum Expenditure Basket (MEB) for food as recommended by the Food Security Cluster. The full MEB for food is €147 (or $159 USD) per household per month, and each household will receive two transfer cycles during the project period, scheduled for January and February 2025. WASH Assistance: Organize hygiene promotion campaigns at the two IDP sites to raise awareness of sanitation, safe water storage, and cholera prevention, thereby reducing disease risk in crowded conditions. Community Engagement: Actively involve IDPs in project activities to foster local ownership and ensure alignment with community needs.
